paragraphs: My name is Lily, and I am ten years old. I wanted a clock for my room. A clock in a shop costs a lot, so I made one. Do you want to make a clock too? You need a white paper plate and a black pen. You also need two sticks of wood and a small metal pin. Take a soft cushion, too. Pip wanted the cushion, so I found another one.

Step one: Write the numbers one to twelve around the plate. Step two: Make all the numbers the same size. Leave enough space between the numbers. Step three: Take a long stick and a short stick. The long stick is for the minutes. The short stick is for the hours. Step four: Put the plate on the cushion. Tom came to look at my work. "The numbers look good," he said.

Step five: Put the two sticks in the middle of the plate. Step six: Push the metal pin through the sticks and the plate. The pin goes into the cushion. Ask Dad to help with the pin. It is sharp, and it can hurt you. Dad held the plate, and I pushed the pin. Now you can move the sticks with your hands.

I moved the sticks to half past four. Pip lay down next to the cushion. His red collar was around his neck. Dad put the clock on the wall of my room. "Is it half past four?" asked Dad. "Yes," I said, "but only for a minute." I will move the sticks again at bedtime. Now my room has a clock from my own hands.
